utterances.text: You are saying that the last two lines -- the last two lines of his answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The last two points that he made in B/C/S are not reflected in the transcript. I do not know whether they were translated into English or not for the persons listening on the English channel. I'm on the live feed, so I listen to both English and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, I'll just put the question to him. The question that was put to you was: "That's why I'm asking you because at page 32, line 4, that's what you said. So if you could clarify what you meant, that would be helpful. When was he mobilised?" What was your answer to that, please, Witness? I'll tell you what is on the transcript. It says: "The same time as I, maybe a few days before. He left town together with Dragan Tomic to Panos when the Uzice Corps arrived." Did you say anything after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Panos. He left from Panos. He was in the rear closer to Serbia, and I was -- I was at my village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you just repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. It's off the screen, but I will just repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The next question, sir, which follows from the question about mobilisation is I would like you to explain to us how one becomes mobilised, if one is mobilised first into the army and then seconded to the reserve police for certain operations, or I'd like you to explain to us how one is mobilised and then becomes a member of the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: What do I know? I mean, they hand out call-up papers. I did not in fact get a call-up paper. I was just hired by Dragan Tomic, and he started assigning me to various tasks. Some other people who were in the police with me, and we were many, did get call-up papers. And then in the police, they formed some platoons - I don't know exactly how it worked - which was the 1st Company, which was the 2nd Company. Some people had been trained to handle a Praga or a tank, but they had already been mobilised into the police, and we were really short of people. Everybody was running away to Serbia. They wanted to keep them there, and they assigned them according to their military evidentiary specialty, you go to operate a tank, you go to man a mortar, because we need those trained people. You couldn't put somebody to operate a mortar or a Praga just like that without training. That's how they went to various assignments, and companies were set up. I don't know how these people who were up there in the authorities handled it. I don't know the exact number, but we were quite a few of us. Then these companies were formed, but many of our men ran away across the border, passing through all the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that the reserve police, the units of the reserve police was part of the Army of the Republika Srpska at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could one be a member of a regular military unit and then also be a reserve police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could one be a reserve police officer and then -- for a certain period of time and then be called up and be mobilised into a unit for a particular military operation? Was there flexibility between the units in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit more detailed? What do you mean by "possibly"? Can you tell us when that would happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, that happened with the police. I mean, I have no clue how these companies were formed then. At that point, much fewer people remained in the police. Many of them went into the army. I was not allowed to go without leave. It's very difficult to explain to you how things worked in the war. It was complicated. Those who don't know from inside wouldn't believe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, in fact I'm one who doesn't -- I don't know from the inside, and I don't believe that the Judges do either. That's why I'm asking you to try to explain it to us. How did it work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, could you ask me a specific question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My specific question was, someone could be recruited into the reserve police force, such as yourself, and then at some point be mobilised into a unit to participate in a particular operation with a military unit. That could happen, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, how shall I explain this to you. If he transferred to the army, he couldn't return back to the police, but we all went together into action: the police, the army, there was no distinction. The artillery would be behind us. We would be going in various groups, one group from here, one group from another side to the same hill to the same objective, and we were all attacking together. The police was hand in hand on the same level as the army, the same uniform, the same everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So during combat, during a combat operation or during some other type of operation, you would know who was a reserve police officer and who was in the military because, as you testified on direct, everyone wore whatever uniform they could find. So is that -- do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: All of them wear camouflage uniforms. For awhile, I had a scouts uniform that I had gotten from Serbia. It had a sort of net here for IC devices so they don't catch you. I mean, I swapped uniforms with one man, and I was allowed to wear that uniform no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But do you agree with what the counsel has put to you, specifically that during a combat operation or some other type of operation, you wouldn't know who was a reserve police officer and who was in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't know. I wouldn't know, and you wouldn't be able to distinguish unless you happen to know the man next to you, but in actions where the reserve police and the army worked together, you wouldn't know just looking at the person whether they were the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us the difference. We've been speaking about reserve police officers. Was there such a group of permanent police officers in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: You mean those who had been in the reserve police even before the war, from before the war? Well, let me think. Tomic, Niko Vujicic, Sredoje Lukic, and Veljko Planicic, perhaps. Then the policemen from Gorazde, the refugees joined in, but when exactly they arrived, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you say those who had been in the reserve police even before the war, well, they wouldn't be called the reserve police, would they? Wouldn't there just be a police department of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation. The witness has testified as to his terms within, and he would be speculating as to things before the war other than his general knowledge. As such, I would say asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't agree. He seems to have a basis for providing the answer. Please answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the question be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The question was, when you say those who had been in the reserve police even before the war, they wouldn't be called the reserve police, would they? Wouldn't they just be the police department of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. Even before the war, they were the reserve police. I don't know in what way they were activated back then, but they were reserve policeman even before the war, but I was not among them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, there were about six police administrations within the Visegrad police department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of administrations you are talking about. There was one administration. The chief was Tomic. I don't know anything about six administrations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that all reserve police officers -- did you have just one building that you reported to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Your Honour, we would ask for a clarification of the record. Page 67, line 16, it's our position that he mentioned both Chief Tomic and also mentioned Perisic. Thank you. Excuse me, line 12, I'm sorry, being the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one quick point. I don't know which is the proper transcript to look at, but on the centre monitors it's line 12 of page 67, but on our private monitors it's line 16. There seems to be a discrepancy of a few lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll move on. It can be corrected after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I would think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So can you tell us then approximately how many reserve police officers there were in this administration in May and June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Quite a few. I don't know the exact number. There should be some records, maybe up to 200, maybe more. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how do you know that there were 200 or maybe more if you didn't -- if you haven't seen any list? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, I know roughly. We couldn't all gather there at the same time. Some men were at Brodar, others were at other locations, but we would run into each other. We know from the talk and sometimes we would sit together and talk and share stories, who had been where, because it's from this number of men that later companies and platoons were formed, and fewer of us remained on the reserve police force attached to the SUP. But even if -- sometimes there could be one single officer on duty remaining in the building because all of us would be raised for an incident to go out in the field and respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say later companies and platoons were formed, when later? When were these companies and platoons formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Sometime in May, beginning of May. Now, who decided on these companies, they had on record everybody's military specialty, who had gotten what kind of training in the army. I was a driver. If they had needed a radar man, I could not have remained on the reserve police force because I would be assigned to a radar, if we had had one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Because I had received training during my military service to operate a radar mounted on a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you said that "... later companies and platoons were formed ... fewer of us remained on the reserve police force ..." then you mentioned later when I asked you specifically when, you said that was sometime in May. So that's your testimony that some men in May, as early as May were being assigned to platoons and other military units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object as to I believe it misstates the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you say is the evidence, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the problem is the vagueness in relation to -- this witness I believe was responding to when they first started being formed into platoons, and then Ms. Sartorio changed the point, and I think it's confusing the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I don't believe it's confusing, Your Honour. I asked a specific follow-up question from a specific answer he gave, and then he gave another answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask the question again, and the witness will answer it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you -- you said that there were fewer police reserves because platoons and units were being formed. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then I asked you, When were these platoons and units being formed, and you said in May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: That's correct I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So as early as May, they were --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know which date in May, but I know it was then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So as early as May, there were some reserve police officers that were being mobilised into military units; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you a little bit about -- first, a question about the exhibit, the photographs that you were shown by the Defence, and I'd like to call up ERN 0213-2844, which -- it was marked for identification 246 last week. And I'd like to go to page 4, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If you could - yes - zoom in on number 59.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the name of this person is next to number 59, what his name is and when he was born and from where and when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: You mean below or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Number 59. If you could just tell us what this says.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: It says Stefan Grujic, born in 1940, born in Koritnik, killed 28th of August, 1992, at Klasnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, this photograph is the same as all the other photographs that you testified to at length on direct examination; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: You mean photographs or the list? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry, that was my fault. You looked at several photographs from this document on direct examination; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the other photographs that you looked at, all the information with regard to those photographs was correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: They are supposed to be correct. Nobody would indicate something incorrect on a tombstone or on a memorial about the dates of killing. I don't know. Maybe those who had been captured, maybe their date of death is not known at all. Who knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But you have no reason to question any of the information that is contained in this document because you testified to a lot of it on direct; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: You mean to challenge the veracity? There was no need, I think. I suppose the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we ask that this page be marked as an exhibit, introduced in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, you -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, I believe --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document P 246 will become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we have to break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'd look to ask you a couple of questions about the incident in Kopito where Mr. Trifkovic was killed. Now, on direct examination you said that soldiers tried to put the fire out with a bottle of water. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I wasn't there, but there was talk about that. I heard it from somebody who was there. They had no mortal remains to bury, and I saw that car, it was bent out completely and had stayed there for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall who told you that the soldiers tried to put the fire out with a bottle of water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Ziga. I can't remember his exact name. I saw his name on the list. He used to work in Sarajevo. He goes by the family name of Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was he a part of any unit during this time, the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: He was a reserve policeman. Whether he was that at that time or in the military, I don't know. He used to be in the reserve police force but not -- I don't know until which point. He had come in his car, and what they tried to do was to put out the fire, but the people had been killed and dead already. He told me that we pulled some water bottles from the cars and tried to put the fire out so that the bodies would no longer burn.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But when you said that he told you that soldiers tried to put out the fire, can you tell us where those soldiers were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, he hailed from there, from Kocarin, to the left of that road. Whether he came from one side or the other side, I don't know. I don't have any idea. Most probably they pulled them out, those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, with regard to some vehicles that were used by the reserve police, it's true, isn't it, that Commander Tomic, when he was killed, he was with Mr. Andric. They were in a white car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't recall the colour of the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, is it true that the police, reserve police force used to use cars or rent cars from a company called Granite; is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know which companies they took vehicles from. It's possible. From companies -- there were Muslim cars, as well, that we used.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And that's my next question. On direct examination at page 36, you said Muslim cars had been requisitioned. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Why only Muslim cars? Why not Serb cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: There were Serb cars most probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But it's your testimony that it was mainly nice cars that were requisitioned; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, misstates the evidence. He made that statement with regards to Tomic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, just reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, was it your memory and your experience that the reserve police officers when they requisitioned cars from Muslims or Serbs, that they tended to requisition cars that were better cars, newer cars than old clunkers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, they could have been older. They were useful for us to go uphill on the non-tarmacked roads, on dirt roads. There were off-road vehicle, Lada Niva. There were older and younger cars. We used very bad roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you if you know a number of people, and if you do know them, in what capacity did you know them? Did you know a person by the name of Mijo Mitrosinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how do you know him, from where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, he was in the intervention company. After the war, we worked our companies were next-door -- our companies were next-door to each other. I informally knew him during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you said he was in the intervention company. Can you please explain for us and the Chamber what you mean by intervention company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Those who went into combat action to capture a summit, irrespective of where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would this be considered a type of special unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. It wasn't special. It wasn't special. Well, we would go on the same task. We would -- they would come from a different part, or they would be split into two groups together with us, and it depended on our arrangements, who was going take which route to the desired goal. But we were together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And the next person is Radomir, otherwise known as Raso, Simic. Do you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Simic, what was his first name? Or was his first name, I'm not sure, Raso or Ramo?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Raso or Radomir. Simsic, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I used to know a Simic who got killed at Soline. I'm not sure whether it was the name of the place, Soline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are talking about Simsic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. My pronunciation is the problem here. I'll repeat. The last name is pronounced Simsic. Simsic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simsic, you mean. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know a person or do you know a person by the name of Dusko Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Ljubisa Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Jovan Lipovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. Where is that Jovan from?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, if you know someone a person by the name of Jovan Lipovac, you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I used to know somebody short, very short. This is how I remembered him. But I didn't know him well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I would notice him on the battle-field. I don't know whether -- when I saw him last, but he is stuck in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But in your memory you saw him on the battle-field when you were on the battle-field; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you know a person or did you know a person by the name of Dobrosav Lipovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the last person is Zoran Mitrosinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I know him. He works in the same company as I.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't know him when it all started, but I met him afterwards. I never went into combat action with him. Now I know him well. We work at the same company. We sit around drinking coffee together, but I don't know when I really met him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And since you know him now, do you know what he did during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, he would go to the battle-fields just as any other combatant.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know what unit or group he was a member of when he went into battle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I think he was in that intervention unit. I'm not sure how it was labelled then, but it was the intervention company. He would go into combat action, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you some questions about the White Eagles that you testified to about on direct. You mentioned that both Muslims and Serbs ran from them. Now, how is it that you knew about the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, one had to get out of their way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what kind of uniforms or what did they wear that made you recognise them as White Eagles so that you could get out of their way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know -- they wore camouflage fatigues, whatever they had. One would wear a sajkaca cap, another would sport a beret. They didn't have uniform uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So they wore the same uniforms as other units that were engaged in combat; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Similar. Similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you know if they had an insignia of a white eagle anywhere on their uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were some insignia, but I'm not sure what kind of insignia they were. On the -- wherever they were attached on their uniform, I can't recall really.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you recall if there was any insignia on the cap that they were wearing or the, as you called it -- well, it's not in the transcript, something on their head. Was there an insignia on whatever they wore on their head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: They wore some, but I'm not sure what kind of insignia those were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I guess then I'm a little confused about how you could get out of their way if you're not able to tell us what there was about them that you would notice in order to get out of their way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, we were more or less all acquainted with one another. We knew that they were in Visegrad. They stood out. People would say, If they are in the hotel, don't get near them, get out of the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you know that Vinko Pandurevic was the commander of the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. I think he wasn't, but I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: They --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Go ahead and finish, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I can't remember what I was about to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you know Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Slightly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In what capacity did you know him? How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I saw him once at Brodar while we were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you saw him, what were you doing? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: We were there --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, this goes beyond the scope of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is our case. We are allowed to put our case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you remember my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, I was at Brodar. There, this was the furthest that we could advance. This was our battle line. I was on a hilltop above the Drina river. We used to bivouac there and sleep there, and these were our forward lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you saw Vinko Pandurevic, you were engaged in an operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, no, no. We were manning this front-line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Was he and his unit manning the front-line with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. His unit was there, yes, some ten men. I didn't know who commanded them. I saw them form a line and being addressed, but I didn't see who. We never were mustered into lines. I was just manning a hilltop above the Drina river.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you know any of these some ten men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I knew a person by the name of Karaklic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Was this person a member of the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No -- Beli Orlovi were not at Brodar, or White Eagles were not at Brodar at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So what unit was Vinko Pandurevic a part of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The commander of what unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation, asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How does it call for -- both of you come from the same jurisdiction, and you have this "asked and answered" thing. What is the speculation here? It seems to me -- was he a member of the White Eagles. Either he knows or he doesn't know. If he doesn't know, he says he doesn't know. What is the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My question, though, was you said: "Well, he was the commander." Was the commander of what, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Troops. Those companies, I don't know how they establish them. There were 10 people or 20 people to a platoon. I don't know. I don't know whether Company 1 was deployed, Company 2. I don't know how they categorised them. I never saw any lists of those troops. People were deployed as per orders that they were given.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you -- can you tell us if you remember the names of any members of this group, the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you remember seeing --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Maybe they sported nicknames, but I can't recall any of them. I had never known their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see them carrying a banner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I can't recall. Maybe, but I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we please -- the court officer please bring up Prosecution's Exhibit 229.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen this banner before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Had you ever seen this skull and cross-bone on any banner or any clothing worn by any person in the reserve police or the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. I don't know about the military, but not in the reserves police. Maybe somebody would sport a badge. There were 10, 20 types of different badges. People would wear badges of all sorts, as far as their fancy took them, but I can't recall seeing this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But as far as you are concerned, no one on the police wore a skull and cross-bone on their uniform, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the caps or the hats that these gentleman are wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I recognise them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And from where do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, the one is sajkaca. Older people would wear such caps, the sajkaca cap in my village. Elderly people sported that headgear.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And is that the gentleman who is on the left as you look at the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, the sajkaca-wearing gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say that older people would wear such cap in your village, is this person -- does this person look -- when you say the older people in the village, are these people that were out in their fields working, or where would you see these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Both going into town or working in the field, maybe an older sajkaca that would be worn if they were working around the household, maybe a newer one would be worn to town, either dark green or blue. In recent years, they wouldn't wear them as frequently as in the olden days. Even today, older people wear sajkacas in my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But sir, it's quite clear from this picture that this gentleman isn't working around the house. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, he is not working around the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the banner says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: With faith in God -- and then I can't make out the bottom, maybe freedom. The rest cannot be made out. With faith in God, freedom or death. It could be freedom or death. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you know any group that used this saying as their motto?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: This photograph may be put away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, as a former reserve police officer, are you aware that between April and August of 1992 that the group the White Eagles were committing crimes in and around the municipality of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know. People used to say that they did, but I didn't see it with my own eyes, so I can't tell you anything about that. The people talked that they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did people talk about any other groups committing crimes against Bosnian civilians during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So just this one group, is that your testimony? Or were there other groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: That one group of White Eagles was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, with regard to Milan Lukic being a member of the reserve police force, are you aware that on the 27th of October of 1992, Mr. Lukic told the Serbian authorities the following. He says: "I have been on the front in Visegrad and its surroundings since 10 April 1992. I am a command commander of the group called the Avengers, initially known as the Obrenovac Detachment. The group has between 20 and 50 men and is under the command of the Visegrad Territorial Defence, and I'm directly subordinate to Vinko Pandurevic." Did you know that Milan made this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we would object to that in terms of hearsay, lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The objection on the ground of hearsay, as you know, doesn't hold water here, Mr. Alarid. Were you aware that Milan Lukic had made such a statement, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, if he had made this statement, could you be mistaken that he was a member of the reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: What do you mean being mistaken to believe that he was in the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, if he made the statement that he was what I just told you he was, as part of the group The Avengers, if he said that and that's true, then are you mistaken that he was part of the reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object in clarification of the transcript. The translation did not pick up his description of his -- Milan Lukic's association with Tomic and Andric. That is not referenced in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to, again, coaching the witness, whatever --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can play the tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The tape will speak for itself later on. You can file your motions objecting to the transcript at another time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer my question whether you might be mistaken that Milan Lukic was part of the reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, is membership of one group incompatible with the other?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is that a question for me? I'll ask the witness that question, and I believe I covered that on direct. Does Your Honour want me to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't have to follow it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, did the police -- were they regularly assigned sniper rifles with silencers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No. But you could carry or bring a sniper rifle if you go into action. But why carry it about every day, because those rifles are heavy. But if you are a good marksmen, then you can bring a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer to please bring up photograph 0644-6594. And if you could bring it up and then zoom in as much as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the men in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I recognise the one on the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you don't know the person on the left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So you didn't know this person to be a member of the reserve police force, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation. He answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, you said you didn't know this person. Had you ever seen this person in any meetings or activities with the reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I do not remember. I may have, but I don't remember his looks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, the picture of Milan Lukic, is this how you remember Milan Lukic looking in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I have never seen him wearing this sort of cap.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But other than the cap, his face, is that how you remember him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: It's been quite awhile. I don't know. It's been 17 years since the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. But you recall him giving you a cigarette in May. So all I'm asking you is did this look like Milan when you knew him during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: But now I can't see what kind of uniform he is wearing in this picture. He seems to be -- have a beard. I've never seen him with a beard, and he is wearing obviously camouflage pants, but this is a civilian jacket or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But can you tell me what you think his approximate age is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He can say --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Irrelevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He can say what he thinks his approximate age is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that he was born in 1967, so I don't have to guess. I know when he was born.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So does he look about 24, 25 in this photograph to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, now, is this the type of cap --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: This is a black and white photograph, so you can't really see him all that well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, is this the type of hat that was routinely worn by reserve police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 249, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like the court officer, please, to bring up 1D 98.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, just for the record could we have Exhibit number. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 249.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies for this -- [microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Nice to hear from you now and then, Mr. Cepic. You are like a forgotten man.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Could we just focus in on the top photo first, please. Sir, did you know a person by the name of Dragutin Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How about a person by the name of Djordje Sevic did you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: As far as you recall, you never knew these men as part of the reserve police officers, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know any of the men in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I know Mijo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And which one is Mijo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: The one on the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The one with the -- looks like a type of a cap and he's got -- well, they all have beards, the one on the right as you look at the photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now may we look at the photograph on the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us if you recognise anyone in this photograph, and if so, tell us whom you recognise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I know Milan, Mijo, and Mitar, three of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say Mijo, I need to ask you, do you know the last name of Mijo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Mitrosinovic. I'm not sure about his first name, but we all called him Mijo. We knew him by the name of Mijo, Mitrosinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And could you describe for us, since we have a transcript here, where Milan is either standing or kneeling down? Can you tell us where he is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: He is standing on the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, on the far left he is standing. Can you tell us who is next to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: It's Mijo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And as far as you are concerned, you don't know any of the other men in this photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, misstates the evidence. He indicated a Mitar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you tell us Mitar, the full name, please, and then describe for the record where Mitar is. What is Mitar's last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know his last name. He is the one standing on the right. That's Mitar. His last name may be Mitrosinovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to make it clear because it's going get confusing. May we assist the witness in marking the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, could you please circle the head of Milan Lukic and put ML next to the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And then, sir, could you circle the person that you knew as Mijo and put -- I believe you said his last name is Mitrosinovic, so put MM?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you also do the same for the person you identified as Mitar, circle his head, please, and just write "Mitar" next to him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, how did you know -- from where did you know this person named Mitar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I knew him because he only had one eye, so -- it was a small town, you know, so that everybody knew people with ... and his brother got killed, so everybody knew these facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Was he a member of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And does this look like the same hat that we saw Milan wearing in the previous photo when he is sitting on the couch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, it looks that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to admit this photograph in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 250, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you a few more questions about this photograph. Do you see the person kneeling down in the middle. He has -- is one of the three men kneeling. He's in the middle, and he's the only one with a beard. Do you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we move up to the photograph at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see this same person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I'm not sure if this is him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The person in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, we'll go back down to the picture at the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, if I told you that the person who was kneeling in the middle has been convicted of war crimes along with Milan Lukic in Belgrade court in 2005, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I can't see the objection to it. But let me ask Ms. Sartorio, how do you plan to get in evidence in relation to this that would be relevant?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm just asking if he knows that, and we will be introducing the judgement if we haven't already. It will be introduced in our case. I'll withdraw the question, Your Honour. I'll withdraw the question. So this document was marked, was it not? Yes. Okay. We may remove this from the screen, and may the court officer please bring up P 230.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, is Milan Lukic wearing a typical uniform worn by a reserve police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I may have had one just like that. He is only in shirt sleeves, but a jacket goes with this shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: As far -- I mean, to the extent it can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have one moment, Your Honour, for a second to consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. This document may be removed from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to ask you some questions now about some other members of the reserve police force. Now, I believe you mentioned these persons on direct, but Dragan Tomic was a member of the police reserve forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What was he a member of, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Well, he was the commander of the police station, and that's what he was before the war. He can't be a reserve police officer if he is a police chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: He was on active police duty. I believe that he graduated from some kind of school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I stand corrected. And Vidoje Andric, was he a member of the reserve police or a member of the regular police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Vidoje Andric was a member of the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what about Risto Perisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: He was chief, but I don't know how that was all agreed. He was a teacher of Serbian, and later on he became chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how about Boban Simsic, Simsic? He was a member of the reserve police force; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: He was but not all the time. Later on, he was transferred to -- I don't know which company. At first he was at Prelovo, and then he went elsewhere and got transferred to a company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the court officer please bring up Prosecution's Exhibit 209.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what the title of this document is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: You want me to read it all out? Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Trebinje Security Services Centre, public security station Visegrad; the 1st of August, 1992; a list of permanent staff and reserve forces of the police; payment of wages for June 1992 permanent staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It says permanent and reserve staff, does it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes. It says permanent -- it says permanent staff, but then at the second mention of permanent staff, there is no mention of reserve forces. Up there, yes, but I'm now looking at the heading with item number 1, marked 1, but the overall title does mention reserve forces of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, my understanding is this document was admitted under seal, so I'm not sure why, but -- we could not publish the document to the public, but I think the questions can be asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, just to run through this quickly, you see number 1 on this first list is Risto Perisic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, I can see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you see number 7 is Dragan Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And number 13 is Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you know that Sredoje Lukic was a member of the police reserves also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: No, he was not in the reserve police. I didn't know him at all. When he was captured, everybody heard of him. It was all over the television by the hydro power-station, the dam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. He was a member of the police prior to the war, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I didn't know him then, but I believe he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, what does it say at the top of the second page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: "Reserve police force." Or you mean the second page?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yeah, you just said what I asked you, at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you move over so the witness can see the numbers, please? Would it be possible? Well, we can't see it on the screen either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This will be the last question, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Just --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you see number 2 is Vidoje Andric?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And number 35 is Boban Simsic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, it says Boban Simsic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, you don't see the name Milan Lukic anywhere on this document that is about payment of wages for June 1992, permanent and reserve police forces, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: I don't know why he isn't on the list. Who knows when the list was made. If this were the original list, he certainly would have been on the list, if the list had been made at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, sir, you see the first page of the list it says 1st of August, 1992, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, lack of foundation, lack of personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: He could look at the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But he can't establish authenticity of it because he never generated it nor did he ever see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I don't understand these objections. Just a minute, please. Just a minute. I don't understand the objections. The first page show the first page, and you are saying the witness can't comment on it because the authenticity can't be established. Is that your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour -- well, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Wouldn't that be apply to all the other questions that have been asked about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. The issue is this, is he has answered the question, he has given his answer as to his speculation with regards to it, and the Prosecution is putting to him something that then now demands the authenticity of the document. His understanding is one thing, but confirming the document as to when it was generated or otherwise is a different thing. It's then offering the document for the truth of the matter asserted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he is not being asked to authenticate the document. What was your question, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, the question was, sir, I'd asked you about various people whom you said were part of the police or the police reserves, and those six names including your own are on this list; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes, my name is on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And Mr. Simsic's name is on the list; Mr. Andric's name is on the list; Mr. Tomic's name is on the list; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD23
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And Milan Lukic's name is not on it, and it is for the Trial Chamber now to deduce what we wish from that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn and resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's just an urgent matter if I could bring to the Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Very quickly. I need to go into private session, Your Honour, to raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.
